title: WASM Target
concept: Compile XIOM to WebAssembly (WASM) — run XIOM code in browsers, Node.js, and any WASM runtime at near-native speed.
why: WASM brings systems programming to the web. XIOM's safety guarantees combined with WASM's sandbox make a potent combination for web applications.
tips: Start with simple functions — arithmetic, string processing — easiest to port to WASM
Use --wasm-bindgen for complex types — automatic JS ↔ XIOM type conversion
WASM binaries can be very small — -Os optimization strips unused code effectively
Test WASM in the browser AND Node.js — behavior differences exist
common_mistakes: Assuming WASM has access to DOM, filesystem, or network — it doesn't without JS glue
Not stripping debug symbols from WASM — adds significant size to the binary
Using XIOM features that don't translate to WASM — threads, file I/O, OS-specific APIs
